Food on the Journey

Experience Afghan food in the places that give it meaning.

Our food and culture notes connect regional dishes and produce to the hubs, markets, restaurants, farms, and cultural experiences where travelers may encounter them. Availability can vary by season and route, so we build appropriate stops into the itinerary when they make sense.

Dishes

The Afghan Table Staples

Countrywide

Aush

Traditional Afghan noodle soup with herbs, legumes, and yogurt. View food note

Countrywide

Aushak

Afghan dumplings filled with leeks and topped with yogurt and lentils. View food note

Countrywide / Regional

Bodana

Succulent, whole-marinated quail skewed and charcoal-grilled over open coals, popular in roadside stops and specialized kabob houses. View food note

Countrywide

Bolani

Thin stuffed flatbread commonly filled with potato or pumpkin. View food note

Countrywide

Chapli Kabob

Large spiced minced meat kabob popular across Afghanistan. View food note

Kunar

Grilled Trout by the Kunar River

Kunar's mountain rivers, forested valleys, and roadside cooking traditions make freshly grilled trout one of the province's most distinctive food experiences. View food note

Herat

Herat Kabob

Regional kabob style associated with Herat’s culinary traditions. View food note

Kabul

Kabul Kabob

Classic grilled kabob commonly served in Kabul restaurants. View food note

Kandahar

Kandahari Rosh

Slow-cooked lamb traditionally served with fresh naan. View food note

Herat

Chicken Korma

Herat-style herb stew with tender meat. View food note

Countrywide

Mantu

Steamed Afghan dumplings topped with yogurt and tomato sauce. View food note

Countrywide

Naan

Traditional Afghan bread baked fresh daily. View food note

Countrywide

Chicken Kabuli

Chicken variation of Kabuli Pulao. View food note

Sar-e Pol / Northern Region

Qawardagh (Qurdagh)

An iconic heritage meat dish of tender beef or lamb slow-seared in its own rich juices and rendered fat, yielding deep savory flavors. View food note

Parwan / Ghorband Valley

Shola-e-Ghorbandi

A rich, savory sticky short-grain rice dish slow-cooked with mung beans, aromatic spices, and meat gravy, finished with garlic-mint chaka (strained yogurt) or melted roghen-e-zard (clarified butter). View food note

Drinks

Tea, Dogh & Refreshment Culture

Hospitality

Dogh

Cold yogurt-based drink often served with meals. View drink note

Hospitality

Green Tea

Widely consumed Afghan green tea traditionally served after meals. View drink note

Hospitality

Saffron Tea

Tea infused with Afghan saffron. View drink note

Hospitality

Sheer Chai

Milk tea popular in Afghan homes and roadside tea houses. View drink note

Badakhshan

Shor Chai of Badakhshan: Tea of the High Mountains

In Badakhshan, warmth matters. Shor chai is a savory tea made with salt, milk, and sometimes butter or cream, designed for mountain climates and long road days. View drink note

Produce

Regional Harvests & Market Identity

Regional

Balkh Melon

Sweet northern melon varieties popular across Afghanistan. View produce note

Regional

Bamyan Potatoes

High-altitude potatoes from Bamyan known throughout the country. View produce note

Panjshir, Parwan, Kabul

Central Valley Mulberries

Iconic sweet white and black mulberries (Toot) enjoyed fresh during late spring or sun-dried into Toot-e-Khoshk, dried mulberries paired with walnuts, for mountain travel snacks year-round. View produce note

Regional

Farah Watermelon

Large watermelons cultivated in western Afghanistan. View produce note

Nangarhar

Jalalabad Sugarcane

Subtropical sugarcane fields supplying fresh-pressed sugarcane juice (Neyshekar) and local jaggery or molasses (Gor) across eastern roadside stalls. View produce note

Regional

Kandahar Grapes

Renowned table grapes from Kandahar vineyards. View produce note

Regional

Kandahar Pomegranate

Ruby red pomegranates famous across Afghanistan. View produce note

Regional

Kunduz Melon

Popular northern melon grown in fertile plains. View produce note

Logar

The Gardens of Logar: Kabul’s Orchard Province

Logar's orchard country is known for gardens and fruit-growing areas that help supply nearby Kabul markets, giving travelers a broader view of the province. View produce note

Regional

Wardak Apples

Wardak apples are one of the province's best-known seasonal products. Orchards in the high valleys produce fruit that appears in local markets during the harvest. View produce note

Regional

Herat Saffron

World-renowned saffron cultivated in Herat Province. View produce note

Paktia

The Pine Nut Harvest of Paktia

Paktia belongs to Afghanistan's pine nut belt. Pine nuts are a prized product, an export item, and a point of regional pride. View dried fruit note

Badghis

The Pistachio Forests of Badghis

Badghis has one of Afghanistan's strongest agricultural identities: pistachios. View dried fruit note

Restaurants, Tea Houses, Markets & Cultural Experiences

Experiences belong to hubs.

Explore food, markets, tea houses, restaurants, and cultural experiences in the hubs where travelers are most likely to encounter them.

Kabul & Kohdaman Valley

Kabul & Kohdaman Valley

Istalif Pottery Village

Historic hillside artisan visits to master potters crafting iconic turquoise-and-green glazed ceramics using natural minerals, wood-fired kilns, and traditional kick wheels.

 Kabul & Kohdaman Valley

Kite Flying & Gudiparan Bazi

Rooftop kite battles, traditional glass-coated string (tar) crafting visits in Shor Bazaar, street snacks, and Friday afternoon cultural gatherings.

 Kabul & Kohdaman Valley

Chashma-e-Dogh

A destination-style food stop that pairs naturally with Kabul itineraries and city planning.

 Kabul & Kohdaman Valley

Bakery Kabul

Chicken Street sweets, crème rolls, cookies, and tea culture connected to Kabul city walks.

Mazar-e-Sharif & Balkh

Mazar-e-Sharif & Balkh

Balkh Carpet Weaving & Loom Workshops

Artisan visits to Turkmen and Northern weaving families producing world-famous hand-knotted Afghan wool carpets (Mauri, Khal Mohammadi) using natural vegetable dyes and traditional loom techniques.

 Mazar-e-Sharif & Balkh

Sol-e-Naw & Spring Traditions

Vernal celebrations around the Holy Shrine of Hazrat Ali and red tulip fields (Gul-e-Sorkh), featuring seasonal spring delicacies like Haft Mewa, Samanak, fresh spinach Bolani, street-side chopan kabob, and hand-churned Sheer Yakh ice cream.

 Mazar-e-Sharif & Balkh

Kabobs, Sweets & Northern Hospitality

Northern culinary traditions connecting street-side shish kabobs with regional desserts, crispy Qatlama Mazari pastry, and sesame halva alongside Buzkashi sports and old-city travel days.

Jalalabad & Eastern Valleys (Nuristan / Nangarhar)

Jalalabad & Eastern Valleys (Nuristan / Nangarhar)

Nuristan Wood Carpentry & Carving

High-mountain artisan encounters exploring centuries-old woodworking traditions, featuring intricate hand-carved cedar pillars, door frames, chest motifs, and indigenous alpine architectural joinery.

 Jalalabad & Eastern Valleys (Nuristan / Nangarhar)

Adam Khan Chapli Kabob & Sugarcane Stops

A Nangarhar food stop that pairs naturally with Jalalabad route days, featuring chapli kabobs paired with fresh-pressed roadside sugarcane juice (Neyshekar).

Herat

Herat

Saffron Tea Houses of Herat

A hospitality experience that pairs hot saffron tea with old-city bazaar walks—featuring seasonal saffron-infused treats like saffron ice cream in summer or saffron candy (nabaat) with saffron tea year-round.

 Herat

Glassblowers of Herat

A cultural craft experience that pairs naturally with Herat food, bazaars, and old city visits.

Kandahar

Kandahar

Pomegranate Orchards & Harvest Walks

A seasonal orchard and market experience built around Kandahar's famous pomegranates and fresh juice stands during autumn months.

 Kandahar

Kandahari Rosh Hospitality Stops

Traditional culinary stops featuring slow-cooked, tender jointed lamb served with fresh hot tandoor naan, onions, and local seasonal sides.

Badakhshan

Badakhshan

Shor Chai Mountain Tea Houses

High-altitude hospitality stops featuring shor chai—a savory, salted tea brewed with milk and butter or cream, served alongside fresh tandoor naan for morning warmth and long mountain road days.

Bamyan

Bamyan

Qurut Markets of Bamyan

A highland dairy-market experience centered on qurut, local trade, and the road between Bamyan City and Band-e-Amir.
